## Verdict

Kelp costs least for a team of 8, at $168 per month. It carries the highest per-seat rate on the list, but its 1-seat minimum is the only one below the team size, so the team pays for exactly the 8 seats it uses. Acme Desk's $11 seat looks cheaper until its 20-seat floor is applied.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $11 | 20 |
| Fennel HQ | $15 | 40 |
| Kelp | $21 | 1 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (8) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Kelp:** minimum 1 is below 8, so 8 seats paid. 8 × $21 = **$168 per month**.
- **Acme Desk:** minimum 20 exceeds 8, so 20 seats paid. 20 × $11 = **$220 per month**. Twelve seats, worth $132, go unused.
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 40 exceeds 8, so 40 seats paid. 40 × $15 = **$600 per month**. Thirty-two seats go unused.

Kelp is $52 per month cheaper than Acme Desk and $432 cheaper than Fennel HQ — $624 and $5,184 over twelve months. Effective rates per person: Kelp $21.00, Acme Desk $27.50, Fennel HQ $75.00.

## Risks

This ranking is unusually fragile, because it rests entirely on the seat minimums rather than on the rates themselves. Kelp has the worst per-seat price on the list and wins only at small headcount. Acme Desk's $220 is fixed until 20 people, so growth to 14 already makes it cheaper than Kelp ($220 against $294), and the gap widens from there. Fennel HQ overtakes Kelp at 29 people. Any hiring plan should be run through these figures before committing.

The price list covers rates and minimums only. Features, support tiers, usage limits and contract length are unstated, so this is a price comparison and not a value judgement. Annual or negotiated terms are not on the list and could reorder the result.
